baseline:
B
A standard transformer block consists of a multi-head self-attention layer followed by a position-wise feedforward network, which is a type of multilayer perceptron (MLP).

B
An MLP is defined by having at least one hidden layer between its input and output layers. The use of non-linear activation functions within these layers is essential, as it allows the network to learn and approximate complex, non-linear functions.

B
The MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron), also called the Position-wise Feed-Forward Network in a transformer, takes the context-aware embeddings from the attention mechanism as its input. It then applies a non-linear transformation to each embedding to further process and transform the information.

C
The MLP's weights are adjusted during training to encode relationships, allowing it to map specific input patterns (keys) to their corresponding learned outputs (values).

C
The weights (W) and biases (b) are the learnable parameters of the model. The training process adjusts these values to encode patterns from the data, effectively "storing" the knowledge. These stored parameters are then used for recall (making predictions).
